Let me set the scene more carefully. The paper introduces what they call selective head retention, abbreviated SHR. The intuition is simple. During training, each attention head accumulates gradient signals, and the magnitude of those signals tells you how much each head contributed to reducing the loss. Heads with consistently small gradient contributions are likely redundant, because removing them would have changed the loss by very little. So at inference time, you can selectively drop those heads. The implementation is just a binary mask over the head dimension.
